financials_interim.notes: Janashakthi Finance PLC (BFN, formerly Orient Finance PLC) is a licensed finance company (NBFI) -- single entity, no Group/Company split. Filing is presented in Rs.'000; all figures below are converted to absolute Rupees (x1,000) for this row, per project convention. shares_in_issue = 211,101,155 ordinary shares, disclosed exactly (Stated Capital note, 'No. of Ordinary Shares'). Cross-checked: EPS 90,413,000/211,101,155 = 0.4283, rounds to disclosed 0.43; NAVPS 4,097,636,000/211,101,155 = 19.41, ties disclosed 19.41 exactly. No column-swap issues found. revenue = 'Total operating income' (933,258,000), the filing's own subtotal = Net interest income (880,373,000) + Fee and commission income (50,045,000) + Other operating income (2,840,000). operating_profit = 'Operating profit/(loss) before Value Added Tax' (212,696,000), the company's own pre-VATFS subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK -- Interest income (1,832,133,000) and Interest expenses (951,760,000) are disclosed as separate gross lines but netted to an explicit 'Net interest income' subtotal before Total operating income (same structure as AFSL/ALLI/AMF/CDB/AAF this session), so populating them separately would double count against revenue. tax_expense = 'Income tax expense' (47,798,000) only; 'Tax on financial services' (74,485,000) is a separate VAT-on-Financial-Services-type levy sitting between operating_profit and profit_before_tax, consistent with this session's other NBFI entries. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split; 'Loans and receivables at amortised cost' (34,450,592,000) is the core lending book across five segments (Finance leases & HP, Loans, Factoring, Gold Loan, Others), not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks - bank overdrafts' (1,417,451,000), explicitly labelled as overdrafts, unambiguously short-term (also confirmed by the cash flow statement's Note A, which nets bank overdrafts of 1,417,451,000 against cash on hand/at bank to reach a NEGATIVE cash-and-equivalents figure of (976,733,000) -- that cash-flow-statement definition is broader than the Balance Sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' line used for cash_and_equivalents below, and is not used here to avoid reporting negative cash). long_term_borrowings = 'Interest bearing borrowings' (14,805,485,000), a separate general borrowings line distinct from the overdraft and from customer deposits; no further maturity split is disclosed on this condensed balance sheet, so this is an approximation (consistent with how this session treated LOFC's undifferentiated borrowings line), cross-checked against the cash flow statement's 'Interest bearing borrowings obtained' (6,800,120,000) and 'Repayment of interest bearing borrowings' (5,621,009,000) during the quarter, which are sizeable roll-overs consistent with structured term funding rather than short-dated facilities. 'Deposits from customers' (18,271,774,000) is deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt, per project convention. 'Lease liability - right of use assets' (445,319,000) is also excluded, consistent with this session's treatment of small lease liabilities for other NBFIs. cash_and_equivalents = Balance Sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' (440,719,000); see above re: the broader, overdraft-inclusive cash-flow-statement definition which nets to a negative figure and is not used here. capex = 'Acquisition of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets' (13,032,000) -- disclosed as a single combined cash-flow line, cannot be disaggregated into PP&E vs intangibles from this filing (a genuine gap, noted below). Impairment/NPL commentary: 'Impairment charges for loans and receivables at amortised cost' rose from Rs.78,388,000 (Q1 FY25/26) to Rs.95,508,000 (Q1 FY26/27), +21.9%, but the segment note (p.5) shows this was NOT broad-based: Gold Loan segment impairment actually fell sharply, from Rs.27,105,000 to just Rs.989,000 (-96%), while the 'Others' segment swung from a Rs.0 impairment charge to Rs.20,068,000 and the core Finance Leases & Hire Purchase segment impairment rose 37% (Rs.47,531,000 to Rs.65,240,000) on a book that grew 32% YoY (segment assets Rs.18,083,894,000 to Rs.23,906,072,000). Depreciation and amortisation also rose sharply, +65% (Rs.48,977,000 to Rs.80,743,000), and Personnel expenses +22% (Rs.225,044,000 to Rs.274,297,000) -- together with the impairment increase, these operating-expense increases explain why Profit before tax rose only 27% (Rs.108,786,000 to Rs.138,211,000) despite Total operating income growing a much stronger 24% and Net interest income growing 26%. The filing itself flags (note 3) that the comparative 31 March 2026 balance sheet figures included here are UNAUDITED and subject to the ongoing year-end audit review process -- a genuine disclosed uncertainty, noted as a gap.

interim_updates.note_text: Janashakthi Finance (BFN, formerly Orient Finance) grew profit faster than income in Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026): Total Operating Income +24% to Rs.933.3mn, Operating Profit before levies +31% to Rs.212.7mn, Profit Before Tax +27% to Rs.138.2mn and PAT +51% to Rs.90.4mn (EPS Rs.0.43 vs Rs.0.28). PAT grew faster than PBT because income tax fell 2% to Rs.47.8mn, cutting the effective tax rate to 34.6% from 44.9%. The income engine is Gold Loans: Gold Loan interest income rose 75% to Rs.708.7mn (Rs.405.2mn), the segment's profit after tax jumped from Rs.13.1mn to Rs.70.7mn -- i.e. Gold Loans alone delivered 78% of group PAT -- and its impairment charge collapsed 96% to Rs.1.0mn from Rs.27.1mn. The legacy Finance Leases & Hire Purchase segment is the opposite: interest income was flat (+2% to Rs.889.5mn) despite segment assets growing 32% to Rs.23.9bn, impairment rose 37% to Rs.65.2mn and segment PAT fell 42% to Rs.24.4mn. The Loans segment more than quadrupled interest income to Rs.195.2mn (Rs.39.9mn) and moved PAT from Rs.0.5mn to Rs.10.8mn, while 'Others' swung to a Rs.15.7mn loss (from +Rs.4.0mn profit) after a Rs.20.1mn impairment charge (nil a year ago). Funding cost took a large bite: Interest Income +35% to Rs.1,832.1mn but Interest Expense +45% to Rs.951.8mn, so Net Interest Income grew +26% to Rs.880.4mn. Fee & Commission Income +35% to Rs.50.0mn; Other Operating Income -80% to Rs.2.8mn. Below income, Impairment Charges +22% to Rs.95.5mn, Personnel +22% to Rs.274.3mn, Depreciation & Amortisation +65% to Rs.80.7mn and Other Operating Expenses +15% to Rs.270.0mn; Tax on Financial Services +39% to Rs.74.5mn. The cost-to-income ratio improved marginally to 67.0% from 67.9%. Balance sheet: total assets +3.6% in the quarter to Rs.39.9bn; loans & receivables +4.5% to Rs.34.5bn; deposits flat (+0.4% to Rs.18.27bn); interest-bearing borrowings +9% to Rs.14.8bn and bank overdrafts up to Rs.1.42bn from Rs.0.84bn. Operating cash flow was -Rs.1,545.0mn (vs -Rs.788.9mn) as the book grew Rs.1.58bn and Rs.617mn of other liabilities were settled; financing inflow +Rs.842.8mn (Rs.6.80bn drawn, Rs.5.62bn repaid). Equity Rs.4,097.6mn (NAV/share Rs.19.41 vs Rs.19.12) after a Rs.29.5mn fair-value loss on government securities; the Rs.36.10 closing price is ~1.86x NAV. Listed on the Second Board with only 6.14% public holding (Janashakthi Ltd 29.9%, People's Bank 25.1%, Bank of Ceylon 14.2%, Sanasa Development Bank 11.5%); LRA rating BB+ (Positive).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no predecessor quarter is stored for BFN (first financial_statements entry). The filing's 31 March 2026 comparative balance sheet is itself UNAUDITED and may be adjusted on completion of the year-end audit. Segment note shows the Loans segment's interest income growing ~4.9x while segment assets grew only 32%; this is as reported and not explained in the filing. Single-entity filing (stored as GROUP).
interim_updates.takeaway: Earnings quality is improving in one place and weak in another: Gold Loans (interest income +75%, PAT 5x, impairment -96%) now carries the company, while the leasing/HP book is growing assets 32% with flat interest income and rising impairment. Funding costs (+45%) are growing faster than yield (+35%), deposits are flat and bank overdrafts are climbing, so the growth is being funded by wholesale debt and negative operating cash flow.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services

operational_highlights: Total Operating Income +24% to Rs.933.3mn; PBT +27% to Rs.138.2mn; PAT +51% to Rs.90.4mn (EPS Rs.0.43 vs Rs.0.28); effective tax rate 34.6% vs 44.9%
Gold Loan segment: interest income +75% to Rs.708.7mn, segment PAT Rs.70.7mn vs Rs.13.1mn (78% of group PAT), impairment -96% to Rs.1.0mn, segment assets +32% to Rs.13.97bn
Finance Leases & Hire Purchase: assets +32% to Rs.23.9bn but interest income only +2% (Rs.889.5mn), impairment +37% to Rs.65.2mn, segment PAT -42% to Rs.24.4mn
Interest Expense +45% (Rs.951.8mn) outran Interest Income +35% (Rs.1,832.1mn); Net Interest Income +26% to Rs.880.4mn
Impairment +22% to Rs.95.5mn, Personnel +22%, Depreciation & Amortisation +65% to Rs.80.7mn; 'Others' segment booked Rs.20.1mn impairment and a Rs.15.7mn loss
Operating cash flow -Rs.1,545.0mn (vs -Rs.788.9mn); borrowings Rs.14.8bn (+9% QoQ), overdrafts Rs.1.42bn (Rs.0.84bn), deposits flat at Rs.18.27bn
NAV/share Rs.19.41; closing price Rs.36.10 (~1.86x NAV); Second Board listing, public holding 6.14%; LRA BB+ (Positive)
key_drivers: Gold Loan boom: segment interest income +75% (Rs.405.2mn to Rs.708.7mn) with impairment cut 96% lifted segment PAT from Rs.13.1mn to Rs.70.7mn -- the main reason group PAT rose 51%
Leasing/HP drag: flat interest income (+2%) on a 32% larger book, impairment +37% and segment PAT -42% (Rs.42.4mn to Rs.24.4mn)
Funding-cost squeeze: Interest Expense +45% vs Interest Income +35%, financed by Rs.6.80bn of new borrowings and a Rs.0.57bn rise in overdrafts
Lower effective tax rate (34.6% vs 44.9%) on Rs.47.8mn tax converted 27% PBT growth into 51% PAT growth
